description:
## Goal

Restore the 00181 public-trace and drain-arbiter budgets after the reactive RuntimeDemand cutover without raising either budget. Eliminate redundant boundary work or duplicate telemetry so the simplification arc is observably smaller under the actual CI coverage configuration.

## Proven regression

Draft PR #118 commit fe73709d44474affa138ec31da058c7c22dcfb24 passed local serial library and fixture gates but CI run 33966002646 failed in the llvm-cov workspace test step:

- compiler2_pull_telemetry_is_bounded_and_keeps_public_trace_signals exceeded 1,600 KiB.
- the_drain_arbiter_publishes_readiness_only_movement_and_attributes_every_evaluation emitted 41 quiescence events against the 34-event ceiling.

Exact matched coverage traces on this machine: green parent 7f2bcc2de emits 2,896 events / 1,576,138 bytes / 34 quiesced; fe73709d4 emits 2,983 / 1,680,956 / 41.

## Corrected causal model, recorded before implementation

The 41 new DeriveRuntimeDemand completions are the visible ordinary formulas introduced by the accepted reactive cutover, not seven proven duplicate executions. Their event-family cost is exactly 82 job-span lines plus 41 work_graph.applied lines. A detached counterfactual changing the initial ExecutableFacts wait from Settled to Current leaves all 2,983 events and 41 quiescence steps unchanged. Predemanding producers merely removes 12 empty initial formula runs and still leaves 41 steps and 1,659,226 bytes, so neither is the causal fix.

The parent and head quiescence traces contain identical non-RuntimeDemand readiness changes: ActivationAnalyzed 10, ReturnType 10, CallSiteSummary 11, ActivationInputs 9, CallSiteTargets 6, Activation 4. Head additionally carries 10 semantically required RuntimeDemand settled flips. One-at-a-time product fact polling distributes those ten changes across seven additional publications. Therefore 34 is an upper bound on arbiter publications, not a demand to erase required RuntimeDemand transitions: the correct construction is to name each product evaluation prerequisite set together and arbitrate its exact settled facts as one drain step, retaining all typed changes and causal wakes.

The public job span and work_graph.applied currently both render World plus the same JobCompletion at successful stop. Existing documentation already defines the job span as the clock and work_graph.applied as the sole causal record across all five completion sites. The corrected ownership contract keeps job start identity, timing, parentage, and exception lifecycle, while successful span stop is payload-free; work_graph.applied retains the full completion and semantic reads exactly once.

## Strategy and acceptance

1. Reproduce from fe73709d4 under actual llvm-cov and compare typed traces with 7f2bcc2de.
2. Add focused REDs for atomic exact-prerequisite arbitration and one-owner completion rendering.
3. Make product producers report their full immediately nameable fact prerequisite set and make the pull driver arbitrate that exact set atomically at a drain. Do not sweep unrelated facts or special-case a fixture/product/fact kind.
4. Keep job spans as timing/identity lifecycle and work_graph.applied as the sole completion/causality payload owner. Do not remove required public events or typed causal fields.
5. Do not increase the 34-event or 1,600-KiB ceilings, restore cone machinery, change work budgets, or special-case fixtures.
6. Preserve fz-kdt.4 ratchets: 1,278 RuntimeDemand evaluations, 1,039 demand changed-revision wakes, 311 demand/construction keys, 1,730 non-demand changed-revision starts, 1,140 non-demand blocked expansions, tree 3 allocations/144 bytes, and semantic artifacts/output.
7. Pass both failing llvm-cov tests, full fz2_cli, focused product/RuntimeDemand/scheduler/telemetry tests, serial library, serial 531-case fixture matrix, cross-process determinism, all-target check, strict clippy, fmt, and diff check.
8. Record before/after counts and remove all diagnostics/scaffolding before review.
title: Eliminate post-RuntimeDemand 00181 telemetry and quiescence budget regression
